import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

rng = np.random.default_rng(2030)
OUT = Path("landing")
DAYS = pd.date_range("2023-01-01", "2025-12-31", freq="D")

# city: (region, share of customers). Shares are rough, informed by SAMA's weekly
# point-of-sale reports, where Riyadh is about a third of card spending.
CITIES = {
    "Riyadh": ("Riyadh", 0.32), "Jeddah": ("Makkah", 0.16), "Makkah": ("Makkah", 0.06),
    "Madinah": ("Madinah", 0.06), "Dammam": ("Eastern Province", 0.07),
    "Khobar": ("Eastern Province", 0.05), "Taif": ("Makkah", 0.04), "Buraydah": ("Qassim", 0.05),
    "Abha": ("Asir", 0.04), "Tabuk": ("Tabuk", 0.04), "Hail": ("Hail", 0.03),
    "Jazan": ("Jazan", 0.04), "Najran": ("Najran", 0.04),
}
CITY_NAMES = list(CITIES)
CITY_W = np.array([w for _, w in CITIES.values()])

# How the e-commerce platform and the branch systems spell the same city
VARIANTS = {
    "Riyadh": ["Riyadh", "الرياض", "RIYADH ", "Riyadh City"],
    "Jeddah": ["Jeddah", "جدة", "Jiddah"],
    "Makkah": ["Makkah", "Mecca", "مكة المكرمة"],
    "Madinah": ["Madinah", "Medina", "المدينة المنورة"],
    "Dammam": ["Dammam", "الدمام"],
}

# category: (SAMA sector, min price, max price, share of lines)
CATEGORIES = {
    "Electronics": ("Electronic and Electric Devices", 150, 6000, 0.18),
    "Clothing & Footwear": ("Clothing and Footwear", 40, 600, 0.25),
    "Furniture": ("Furniture", 300, 8000, 0.07),
    "Food & Beverages": ("Beverage and Food", 5, 150, 0.30),
    "Jewelry": ("Jewelry", 200, 15000, 0.05),
    "Health & Beauty": ("Health", 15, 400, 0.15),
}
CATS = list(CATEGORIES)

# Approximate Gregorian dates; Hijri dates depend on moon sighting
EVENTS = [
    ("Ramadan", "2023-03-23", "2023-04-20"), ("Ramadan", "2024-03-11", "2024-04-09"),
    ("Ramadan", "2025-03-01", "2025-03-29"),
    ("Eid al-Fitr", "2023-04-21", "2023-04-24"), ("Eid al-Fitr", "2024-04-10", "2024-04-13"),
    ("Eid al-Fitr", "2025-03-30", "2025-04-02"),
    ("Eid al-Adha", "2023-06-28", "2023-07-01"), ("Eid al-Adha", "2024-06-16", "2024-06-19"),
    ("Eid al-Adha", "2025-06-06", "2025-06-09"),
    ("White Friday", "2023-11-20", "2023-11-27"), ("White Friday", "2024-11-25", "2024-12-02"),
    ("White Friday", "2025-11-24", "2025-12-01"),
    ("National Day", "2023-09-20", "2023-09-26"), ("National Day", "2024-09-20", "2024-09-26"),
    ("National Day", "2025-09-20", "2025-09-26"),
    ("Back to School", "2023-08-06", "2023-08-19"), ("Back to School", "2024-08-04", "2024-08-17"),
    ("Back to School", "2025-08-10", "2025-08-23"),
]
EVENTS = [(n, pd.Timestamp(a), pd.Timestamp(b)) for n, a, b in EVENTS]

def day_factors(day):
    total = {3: 1.15, 4: 1.2, 5: 1.1}.get(day.weekday(), 0.95)   # Thu, Fri, Sat busiest
    if day.day >= 27 or day.day <= 2:
        total *= 1.25                                              # salaries paid around the 27th
    cat = {c: 1.0 for c in CATS}
    for name, a, b in EVENTS:
        if not (a <= day <= b):
            continue
        if name == "Ramadan":
            total *= 1.3
            cat["Food & Beverages"] *= 1.6
            if day >= b - pd.Timedelta(days=10):                   # pre-Eid shopping
                cat["Clothing & Footwear"] *= 2.0
                cat["Jewelry"] *= 1.8
        elif name == "White Friday":
            total *= 1.8
            cat["Electronics"] *= 2.5
        elif name == "National Day":
            total *= 1.4
        elif name == "Back to School":
            cat["Clothing & Footwear"] *= 1.5
    return total, cat

# Reference data
customers = pd.DataFrame({
    "customer_id": [f"C{i:05d}" for i in range(1, 20001)],
    "home_city": rng.choice(CITY_NAMES, 20000, p=CITY_W),
})

product_rows = []
for i in range(1, 401):
    c = rng.choice(CATS, p=[CATEGORIES[k][3] for k in CATS])
    lo, hi = CATEGORIES[c][1], CATEGORIES[c][2]
    product_rows.append({"product_id": f"P{i:04d}", "category": c,
                         "brand": f"Brand {rng.integers(1, 41)}",
                         "list_price_sar": round(float(rng.uniform(lo, hi)), 2)})
products = pd.DataFrame(product_rows)
PROD_IDS = {c: products.loc[products.category == c, "product_id"].to_numpy() for c in CATS}
PROD_PRICE = {c: products.loc[products.category == c, "list_price_sar"].to_numpy() for c in CATS}

branch_cities = ["Riyadh"] * 6 + ["Jeddah"] * 4 + ["Dammam", "Khobar", "Makkah", "Madinah",
                 "Taif", "Buraydah", "Abha", "Tabuk", "Hail", "Jazan", "Najran"]
branches = pd.DataFrame({"branch_id": [f"B{i:02d}" for i in range(1, len(branch_cities) + 1)],
                         "city": branch_cities})
branches["region"] = branches.city.map(lambda c: CITIES[c][0])
BRANCHES_IN = {c: branches.loc[branches.city == c, "branch_id"].to_numpy() for c in CITY_NAMES}
branches = pd.concat([branches, pd.DataFrame([{"branch_id": "WEB", "city": "Online", "region": "Online"}])])

HOUR_W = np.array([2, 1, 1, .5, .5, .5, .5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 10, 8, 5])
HOUR_W = HOUR_W / HOUR_W.sum()                                    # evening peak
METHODS = ["mada", "Apple Pay", "Visa/Mastercard", "STC Pay", "Tabby", "Tamara", "Cash on Delivery"]
PAY_ONLINE = [.45, .20, .12, .04, .08, .05, .06]
PAY_STORE = [.55, .22, .15, .04, .02, .02, .00]

# Orders
orders, items, payments = [], [], []
cust_ids, cust_city = customers.customer_id.to_numpy(), customers.home_city.to_numpy()
n = 0
for d, day in enumerate(DAYS):
    total, cat_mult = day_factors(day)
    w = np.array([CATEGORIES[c][3] * cat_mult[c] for c in CATS])
    w = w / w.sum()
    for _ in range(rng.poisson(110 * total * 1.01 ** (d / 30))):   # ~1% monthly growth
        n += 1
        oid, ci = f"O{n:07d}", rng.integers(len(cust_ids))
        city, online = cust_city[ci], rng.random() < 0.4
        local = BRANCHES_IN.get(city, np.array([]))
        branch = "WEB" if online or len(local) == 0 else rng.choice(local)
        ts = day + pd.Timedelta(hours=int(rng.choice(24, p=HOUR_W)), minutes=int(rng.integers(60)))
        status = rng.choice(["delivered", "cancelled", "returned"], p=[.93, .04, .03])
        gross = 0.0
        for line in range(1, int(rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4], p=[.55, .25, .13, .07])) + 1):
            c = rng.choice(CATS, p=w)
            k = rng.integers(len(PROD_IDS[c]))
            qty, price = int(rng.choice([1, 1, 1, 2, 3])), PROD_PRICE[c][k]
            discount = round(price * qty * rng.choice([0, 0, 0, .1, .2]), 2)
            vat = round((price * qty - discount) * 0.15, 2)              # 15% VAT
            items.append((oid, line, PROD_IDS[c][k], qty, price, discount, vat))
            gross += price * qty - discount + vat
        method = rng.choice(METHODS, p=PAY_ONLINE if online else PAY_STORE)
        payments.append((oid, 1, method, 4 if method in ("Tabby", "Tamara") else 1, round(gross, 2)))
        orders.append((oid, cust_ids[ci], branch, "Online" if online else "Store",
                       rng.choice(VARIANTS.get(city, [city])), ts, status))

orders = pd.DataFrame(orders, columns=["order_id", "customer_id", "branch_id", "channel",
                                       "city", "order_ts", "status"])
items = pd.DataFrame(items, columns=["order_id", "line_no", "product_id", "quantity",
                                     "unit_price_sar", "discount_sar", "vat_sar"])
payments = pd.DataFrame(payments, columns=["order_id", "payment_seq", "payment_method",
                                           "installments", "amount_sar"])

# Monthly files, with the mess real exports have
month = orders.order_ts.dt.strftime("%Y-%m")
for ym, mo in orders.groupby(month):
    folder = OUT / "sales" / ym
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    mo = mo.copy()
    fmt = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M" if ym == "2024-07" else "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"   # a system upgrade
    mo["order_ts"] = mo.order_ts.dt.strftime(fmt)
    ids = set(mo.order_id)
    month_items = items[items.order_id.isin(ids)]
    month_items = pd.concat([month_items, month_items.sample(frac=0.005, random_state=1)])  # duplicates
    mo.to_csv(folder / "orders.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
    month_items.to_csv(folder / "order_items.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
    payments[payments.order_id.isin(ids)].to_csv(folder / "payments.csv", index=False,
                                                encoding="utf-8-sig")

ref = OUT / "reference"
ref.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
customers.to_csv(ref / "customers.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
products.to_csv(ref / "products.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
branches.to_csv(ref / "branches.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
pd.DataFrame([(c, v[0]) for c, v in CATEGORIES.items()], columns=["category", "sama_sector"]) \
  .to_csv(ref / "category_sector_map.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")
pd.DataFrame([(nm, a.date(), b.date()) for nm, a, b in EVENTS],
             columns=["event_name", "start_date", "end_date"]) \
  .to_csv(ref / "events.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig")

print(f"{len(orders):,} orders, {len(items):,} lines, {month.nunique()} months")

import re
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

def read_raw_csv(path, sep=","):
    df = (spark.read
          .option("header", True)
          .option("sep", sep)
          .option("multiLine", True)
          .option("escape", '"')
          .option("encoding", "UTF-8")
          .csv(path))                            # everything stays text in bronze
    # The BOM sticks to the first column name (order_id), so clean every name
    BOM = chr(0xFEFF)   # the invisible byte order mark
    clean_names = []
    for name in df.columns:
        clean_names.append(name.replace(BOM, "").strip())   # drop the mark and spaces
    return df.toDF(*clean_names)                              # rename the columns

def audit(df):
    # Add two columns so every row says where and when it was loaded
    df = df.withColumn("_source_file", F.input_file_name())    # which file it came from
    df = df.withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())  # when it was loaded
    return df

def snake(name):
    # Turn a header like "Sales (SAR) / Month" into "sales_sar_month"
    name = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zA-Z]+", "_", name)   # anything not a letter or digit -> _
    name = name.strip("_")                        # no _ at the start or end
    return name.lower()                           # all lower case

def clean_orders(df):
    out = df.select(
        F.trim("order_id").alias("order_id"),
        F.trim("customer_id").alias("customer_id"),
        F.trim("branch_id").alias("branch_id"),
        F.trim("channel").alias("channel"),
        standard_city("city").alias("city"),
        parse_ts("order_ts").alias("ordered_at"),     # Riyadh local time
        F.lower(F.trim("status")).alias("status"),
        "_ingested_at",
        "_load_month",      # the bronze month this row came from (needed to sync deletes)
    )
    return keep_latest(out, ["order_id"]).withColumn("order_date", F.to_date("ordered_at"))

def clean_order_items(df):
    out = df.select(
        "order_id",
        F.col("line_no").cast("int").alias("line_no"),
        "product_id",
        F.col("quantity").cast("int").alias("quantity"),
        money("unit_price_sar").alias("unit_price_sar"),
        money("discount_sar").alias("discount_sar"),
        money("vat_sar").alias("vat_sar"),
        "_ingested_at",
        "_load_month",
    )
    out = keep_latest(out, ["order_id", "line_no"])          # removes the duplicate lines
    net = (F.col("unit_price_sar") * F.col("quantity") - F.col("discount_sar")).cast("decimal(12,2)")
    return (out.withColumn("net_sales_sar", net)
               .withColumn("gross_sales_sar", (net + F.col("vat_sar")).cast("decimal(12,2)")))

def clean_payments(df):
    out = df.select(
        "order_id",
        F.col("payment_seq").cast("int").alias("payment_seq"),
        F.trim("payment_method").alias("payment_method"),
        F.col("installments").cast("int").alias("installments"),
        money("amount_sar").alias("amount_sar"),
        "_ingested_at",

from delta.tables import DeltaTable

START = "1900-01-01 00:00:00"   # "never loaded": older than any real data


def upsert(df, target, keys, sync_months=None):
    """Update rows whose keys already exist in target, add rows whose keys are new.
    sync_months: the _load_month values that df contains in full. Rows of those months
    that are in target but missing from df were removed at the source, so they are deleted."""
    # First run: the table doesn't exist yet, so just create it
    if not spark.catalog.tableExists(target):
        df.write.format("delta").saveAsTable(target)
        return

    # Build the match rule, e.g. "t.order_id = s.order_id AND t.line_no = s.line_no"
    # t = the existing table, s = the new rows
    conditions = []
    for k in keys:
        conditions.append(f"t.{k} = s.{k}")
    condition = " AND ".join(conditions)

    target_table = DeltaTable.forName(spark, target)
    merge = (target_table.alias("t")
        .merge(df.alias("s"), condition)
        .whenMatchedUpdateAll()       # key found  -> overwrite that row
        .whenNotMatchedInsertAll())   # key is new -> add the row

    if sync_months:
        # Key in target but not in the batch -> delete it, but ONLY within the batch's months.
        # Other months are simply not in this batch; without this condition they would all be wiped.
        month_list = ", ".join(f"'{m}'" for m in sync_months)
        merge = merge.whenNotMatchedBySourceDelete(condition=f"t._load_month IN ({month_list})")

    merge.execute()


def get_watermark(table):
    """Return the newest timestamp already loaded for this table."""
    if not spark.catalog.tableExists("etl_watermark"):
        return START                                  # nothing loaded yet
    rows = spark.table("etl_watermark").filter(F.col("table_name") == table)
    row = rows.select("last_value").first()          # None if this table has no bookmark
    if row is None:
        return START
    return row["last_value"]


def set_watermark(table, value):
    """Save the new bookmark for this table (one row: table_name, last_value)."""
    df = spark.createDataFrame([(table, str(value))], "table_name string, last_value string")
    upsert(df, "etl_watermark", ["table_name"])   # replaces the old bookmark

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

t = spark.table
results = []

def check(name, failing_rows):
    results.append((name, int(failing_rows), failing_rows == 0, datetime.now(timezone.utc)))

lines, orders = t("gold_fact_sales_lines"), t("gold_fact_orders")
CITIES = ["Riyadh", "Jeddah", "Makkah", "Madinah", "Dammam", "Khobar", "Taif",
          "Buraydah", "Abha", "Tabuk", "Hail", "Jazan", "Najran"]

# 1. Keys are unique and present
check("lines_pk_unique", lines.groupBy("order_id", "line_no").count().filter("count > 1").count())
check("orders_pk_unique", orders.groupBy("order_id").count().filter("count > 1").count())
check("lines_keys_not_null", lines.filter(F.col("product_key").isNull() | F.col("date_key").isNull()).count())

# 2. Every line finds its product, branch and date
check("lines_product_exists", lines.join(t("gold_dim_product"), "product_key", "left_anti").count())
check("lines_branch_exists", lines.join(t("gold_dim_branch"), "branch_key", "left_anti").count())
check("lines_date_exists", lines.join(t("gold_dim_date"), "date_key", "left_anti").count())

# 3. Standardized values: only the 13 known cities, no unparsed timestamps
check("city_is_standard", orders.filter(~F.col("city").isin(CITIES)).count())
check("order_hour_parsed", orders.filter(F.col("order_hour").isNull()).count())

# 4. Saudi VAT: 15% of net sales, allowing 1 halala of rounding per line
check("vat_is_15_percent",
      lines.filter(F.abs(F.col("vat_sar") - F.col("net_sales_sar") * 0.15) > 0.01).count())

# 5. Each payment equals its order's total including VAT (within 0.05 SAR)
check("payment_matches_order",
      orders.filter(F.abs(F.col("amount_paid_sar") - F.col("order_gross_sar")) > 0.05).count())

# 6. Net sales reconcile between silver and gold
silver_total = t("silver_order_items").agg(F.sum("net_sales_sar")).first()[0]
gold_total = lines.agg(F.sum("net_sales_sar")).first()[0]
check("net_sales_reconcile", 0 if silver_total == gold_total else 1)

# 7. Market data covers every category
check("market_covers_categories",
      t("gold_dim_category").join(t("gold_fact_market_monthly"), "category", "left_anti").count())

report = spark.createDataFrame(results, "check_name string, failing_rows long, passed boolean, checked_at timestamp")
report.write.format("delta").mode("append").saveAsTable("dq_results")
report.show(truncate=False)

failed = [r[0] for r in results if not r[2]]
if failed:
    raise Exception(f"Data quality checks failed: {failed}")

Why these checks, and not end-to-end runs?

Fabric notebooks run on Fabric capacity, so running the whole pipeline inside GitHub Actions is complex and slow. The split is deliberate: CI catches code and contract problems before merging, and the data quality notebook from Step 8 checks the real data on every scheduled run. Saying this in an interview shows you know where each kind of test belongs.
Python library can deploy the items in your repo to a target workspace from a GitHub Actions job, so merging to

intro_sections.title: The story
intro_sections.lead: Waha Retail (fictional) sells electronics, clothing, furniture, food, jewelry and health products through 25 branches across the Kingdom and an online store.
intro_sections.text: Every month, finance merges point-of-sale and e-commerce exports by hand in Excel. They want a dashboard that updates itself, shows sales by city, channel and payment method, and measures Ramadan, White Friday and National Day.
intro_sections.quote: Are we growing faster or slower than the market?
intro_sections.tip: Use this story in your README and client proposals.

side.title: The benchmark idea: index both to 100
side.caption: Illustration only. The guide compares the retailer with real SAMA card spending, indexed to 100 so growth is compared like for like.

cards.title: The retailer's data
cards.text: No public Saudi dataset has individual orders, so a Python script you run once creates three years of realistic monthly files.
bullets: Orders, order lines, payments, customers, products, branches
SAR prices with 15% VAT; mada, Apple Pay, STC Pay, Tabby, Tamara
Fri–Sat weekends, salary-day peaks around the 27th, seasonal spikes
Real-world mess on purpose: Arabic + English city names, a timestamp format change, duplicate lines, byte order marks

cards.title: The market benchmark
cards.text: SAMA publishes point-of-sale card spending by sector; KAPSARC republishes it as Points of Sale Transactions and Sales by Sector.
bullets: Sectors such as clothing, furniture, jewelry, electronics, food and health
Your pipeline downloads it automatically and lines it up with the retailer's categories

intro_sections.title: Be transparent in your portfolio
intro_sections.text: Say the retailer is fictional and its data generated, and that the market data is real and published by SAMA. Clients respect that, and the generator itself shows skill.
